Section 17.2 carries exactly one scanner-visible obligation, clause 17.2#1: a reader MAY retain an unknown event as inert history but MUST NOT derive state from it. Two of the seven Section 15.1 clauses stay unimplemented here. Clause 15.1#5 is the RPC hello obligation - an error contract key must never be advertised or negotiated in a hello frame - and New builds a failure object rather than a hello frame; this repository contains no RPC hello builder at all, so BindingFor is a static table with no negotiation path rather than a refusal of one. Clause 15.1#6 is the Provider JSON-over-stdio bootstrap row, whose only RFC 2119 sentence is that the plugin MUST NOT masquerade a different-major object as v2; that obligation binds the provider plugin and this repository builds no provider plugin, only the cataloggen and tracecheck binaries. LocalFromUntrusted implements the host half of the same row, but that half states no RFC 2119 keyword, so it discharges nothing the clause scanner measures and is claimed for clause 15.1#7 instead.

ownership.gap: Section 15.2 states its eighteen-row exit-code registry as a table with no RFC 2119 keyword, so the clause scanner measures zero obligations and ExitCodeFor cannot discharge a clause this gate can see. The table is implemented and checked row for row against the pinned text - TestExitStatusRegistryMatchesThePinnedTableRowForRow measures the row count and every status from internal/specdoc rather than restating them - and internal/cliresult now maps a failure to that exact process status through Emit and ExitStatus. What is still missing is the process itself: this repository builds no ax binary, and the only os.Exit calls in the tree are the exit(1) failure paths of cataloggen and tracecheck, so nothing here ever terminates with a Section 15.2 status.

Clause 15.3#3 additionally forbids Structured Error from appearing as an RPC hello key or a TerminalBackend capability, and ExitCodeFor resolves a code-to-exit mapping rather than building either advertisement. No RPC hello frame and no TerminalBackend capability set is built anywhere in this repository, so Section 15.3 keeps that clause unimplemented.

ownership.gap: One of the nine Section 14.2 clauses stays unimplemented here. Clause 14.2#6 requires the process exit status to equal the failure object's exit_code. Emit resolves that exact status from the Structured Error registry and returns it, and ExitStatus reports it without emitting, but this repository builds no ax binary: the only os.Exit calls in the tree are the exit(1) failure paths of cataloggen and tracecheck, so no process in this repository ever terminates with a CLI failure status and the process-level half of 14.2#6 is unowned. Read checks the same equality from the consuming side and refuses an invocation whose failure object and observed status disagree, which narrows the gap to the missing process and does not close it. The other eight clauses are discharged - the common flag set, the --yes admission rule, the one-JSON-document boundary, the destructive-operation confirmation and expectation-flag rules, the rpc serve --json refusal, and the takeover adoption rule.

unowned_sections.gap: Section 2.2 states the unconditional lease, replica, replication, tombstone and capability invariants of the product, and none of them is implemented here. The binding this entry replaces named validateSessionRecordCommon, which validates Session Record shape and the execution-profile enum value only.
unowned_sections.evidence: The repository contains no lease, epoch, replica, takeover, tombstone or replication implementation: internal/canonicaljson validates record shape, internal/localstore stores immutable objects and rebuilds a local index, and the two acceptance cases the replaced binding named are canonical-identity cases.
